errors.english: motivated solely by compassion for worldly beings, they engage in outward conduct
errors.why: The root verse says the Buddhas, solely with a worldly understanding (lokabuddhyā), engage in the consideration of external things (phyi rol spyod = bāhyacintā); there is no compassion here and no 'outward conduct'.

fix.find: motivated solely by compassion for worldly beings, they engage in outward conduct
fix.replace: solely with a worldly understanding, they engage in the consideration of external objects

errors.english: [note: Tibetan: (glang chen gzigs stangs), Sanskrit: (nāgāvalokita), referring to the solemn, direct gaze of a Buddha turning the whole body]
errors.why: Here the image is PV's gajanimīlana, the elephant's closing of the eyes, i.e. seeing but acting as if not seeing, as the commentary itself explains; the nāgāvalokita gloss misleads.

fix.find: [note: Tibetan: (glang chen gzigs stangs), Sanskrit: (nāgāvalokita), referring to the solemn, direct gaze of a Buddha turning the whole body]
fix.replace: [note: Tibetan: (glang chen gzigs stangs), Sanskrit: (gajanimīlana), the elephant's closing of the eyes: seeing, yet acting as if one does not see]

errors.english: If one asks: who are those who are not endowed with the nature of reality
errors.why: The root verse says reality is not appropriate (to be known) — by whom? by all who do not see the supreme; it is not about persons 'not endowed with the nature of reality'.

note: Commentary on Pramāṇavārttika perception chapter mostly followed, but the root verse on the Buddhas' worldly-minded analysis is mistranslated and the elephant image is wrongly glossed.

errors.english: For if the ascertainment of identity with it and of arising from it follows upon it
errors.why: It is the capacity to make known that follows upon the ascertainment of identity and causal arising, not the ascertainment that follows upon something (as the next sentence, correctly rendered, confirms).

note: Close, literal rendering of Śākyabuddhi's argument on conjunction-based reasons; one inverted subject, plus some unmarked explanatory glosses in parentheses.

errors.english: (concordance) invariable presence in similar cases
errors.why: Here rjes su 'gro ba is the universal's extending through its instances, not the logical anvaya (presence in similar cases).

note: A terse lemma-by-lemma commentary rendered serviceably; the debate on universals and their manifestation is followed.

errors.english: just as universals and manifestations cannot be
errors.why: spyi gsal ba dpyod pa'i skabs su (continuing on the next side) means 'in the section examining the manifestation of universals', where this was already explained; it is not a comparison with universals and manifestations.

fix.find: just as universals and manifestations cannot be
fix.replace: as [already explained] in the examination of the manifestation of universals

errors.english: because they are intended to establish convention in just such a way
errors.why: The result follows from the intention of the convention-maker (the one who institutes the mantra), who intends it thus.

errors.english: transforming the mental continuum
errors.why: The continuum that transforms is the mantra's own series of moments; 'mental' is not in the text and shifts the argument.

note: The anti-Mīmāṃsā argument on mantra efficacy is generally followed; a misparsed cross-reference at the end and two smaller slips.

errors.english: when grasping what appears to the mind as reality
errors.why: de kho na zhes bya ba marks a cited word ('just that' / 'only'), not 'reality' (tattva).

errors.english: Not understanding the intention of others
errors.why: gzhan gyis is ergative: the other party, not understanding [the author's] intention, said 'the externals' etc.

note: Sound rendering of the apoha discussion of conceptual cognition and svalakṣaṇa; minor misreadings of lemma markers.

errors.english: what the causes and conditions of transformation are
errors.why: 'gyur ba completes the clause begun on the previous side (sems can rnams kyi rnam par dag par 'gyur ba): the causes and conditions by which beings become purified, not of 'transformation'.

fix.find: what the causes and conditions of transformation are
fix.replace: what the causes and conditions are by which sentient beings become purified

errors.english: meditative absorption (samadhi) is shown as the entry, and the entry is shown as meditative absorption
errors.why: snyoms par 'jug pa is samāpatti (meditative attainment), not 'the entry'.

errors.english: They are the voice of another [note: instruction from a teacher]
errors.why: The qualifier rjes su mthun pa (conducive, favourable) of the other's voice (parataḥ ghoṣa) is dropped.

note: The sūtra quotation on the Tathāgata's knowledge of causes of defilement and purification and of the meditative attainments is largely accurate.

errors.english: One should turn both oneself and others away from what is not harmful.
errors.why: gnod pa las ... bzlog par bya: one should turn oneself and others away from what is harmful.

fix.find: away from what is not harmful

errors.english: the remainderless state [note: referring to nirvana with remainder]
errors.why: lhag ma lus pa is 'with remainder'; the two kinds are nirvāṇa with remainder and without remainder, and the English calls the first 'remainderless' while its note says the opposite.

fix.find: the remainderless state [note: referring to nirvana with remainder]

errors.english: serpent deity Jogpo
errors.why: 'Jog po is the standard Tibetan for the nāga king Takṣaka; the Tibetan should not be left as a pseudo-name.

note: Prefatory purpose-and-connection section of a Bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa commentary; the argument is followed but there is a negation reversal and two term errors.

errors.english: the object of cognition and the negation of that object are designated as existing because they are present, while their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception. Thus, even the perceived is said to be non-existent.
errors.why: The cognition and its object, which is the thing to be negated, exist by being designated existent; their absence is the absence that is non-perception, hence it is called 'absence of perception' (dmigs pa med pa).

fix.find: the object of cognition and the negation of that object are designated as existing because they are present, while their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception. Thus, even the perceived is said to be non-existent.
fix.replace: the cognition and its object, which is the thing to be negated, exist in that they are designated as existent, and their absence is the absence that is non-perception. Hence it is called "absence of perception."

errors.english: by using signs that are not incompatible with the body or the mind
errors.why: The Mīmāṃsakas argue from body, mind and the like, which are not incompatible with omniscience etc.; the English makes body and mind the things the signs are compatible with.

fix.find: by using signs that are not incompatible with the body or the mind
fix.replace: by using properties such as body and mind, which are not incompatible with omniscience and so forth

errors.english: it is affected by the transformative power of the object or the sense faculties
errors.why: It is the object or the faculty that is affected by a (supernormal) empowering force, not a power belonging to the object or faculty.

note: Discussion of non-perception and the final causal complex; the core definition of non-perception and the anti-Mīmāṃsaka sentence are garbled.

errors.english: Regarding that which relates to the essential nature of the (dharmin) subject
errors.why: In this list of contradictory reasons (cf. chos kyi rang gi ngo bo dang 'gal ba just before), 'brel ba stands for 'gal ba: the reason that contradicts the subject's own nature.

note: Careful rendering of the commentary on svayam and iṣṭa in the thesis definition; one term follows a scribal reading instead of the evident sense.

errors.english: but they do not cease to belong to the category of reasons in that sense
errors.why: The point is that deviant similarity and dissimilarity statements do not come to count as reasons, since the general rule has no scope in the exception's domain; the English implies they remain reasons.

note: Verses and prose of the debate on qualifying the statement of similarity are well segmented and largely accurate.
